subject: suggest a function that can consecutively save posterior samples before all iteration finished

messages.author: f11b52e0e4d4a168
messages.subject: suggest a function that can consecutively save posterior samples before all iteration finished
parts:
For a large project, it may takes long time to get model converge. If stan can  consecutively save posterior samples before all iteration finished, we can check results early.

for example, the prespecified iteration is 1000, then we can let stan to save result at 200, 400, ...,1000 iteration.

In this way, we may get the desired result without waiting all iteration finished. Or, we can start to compile a new model, if we suspected the model will never converge even all iteration finished.

Is it possible for stan to have this function?

Thanks

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] suggest a function that can consecutively save posterior samples before all iteration finished
parts:
We are going to allow restarts in Stan 3 (no release schedule yet,
but hopefully during early 2015).

Even with the functionality to restart, there is an issue with
warmup. Until convergence of the warmup estimates (step size and
mass matrix), it's no use running more sampling iterations. After
warmup has converged, restarting should be no problem.

We're not sure we're going to have exactly reproducible results
from running and saving and restarting --- it will have to round-trip
the double-precision floating-point values through I/O, which we think we
can get right, and also has to save and restart the random number generator
(which will require rewriting our config because restarting is a different
config than seeding with the PRNG we're using).

- Bob

messages.author: 54788cf3a8eb8916
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] suggest a function that can consecutively save posterior samples before all iteration finished
parts:
I might have misunderstood you, but you can use the print statement to see particular values (even calculated values) at every iteration - refer section "24.8 Print Statements" in the Stan 2.5 reference manual p.254.

However, if you print something inside in a loop every iteration it will kill your speed quite dramatically - you might want to refer to the "Print Frequency" section.  I'm afraid I don't know how to access the chain iteration counter - perhaps you can count yourself?

In the past I have used this for some very tedious debugging of a rare event.

Sean

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] suggest a function that can consecutively save posterior samples before all iteration finished
parts:
I mean to SAVE the posterior samples BEFORE all iteration finished. It will not slow down the computation because the saving is on few times(like 25% or 50% of all iterations), not every iteration.

The print function only can see particular values, it will not tell us the summary results. while, if we can save the samples, we can do much more analysis.

In my project, it usually takes few weeks to get the results. If we can have the posterior samples before all iteration finished, we can make early design ( change the model or extend the iteration).

I have tried to restart, but the new iteration seems different than previous one and still need to waste time on warmup.

How many effective samples do you need?

Lee,

If you look at the 8schools model and run it normally it doesn't print anything until the end.  If I add some Stan print statements in the middle of the model then it will print out values to the console as it goes along - it is less than what you want - but it works now.  Refer to the reference manual for more details.  Note again this is Stan syntax not R.  Try running this - it should only take a few seconds since it is small...

8schools-modified.stan
data {
  int<lower=0>J; // number of schools
  real y[J];     // estimated treatment effects
  real<lower=0> sigma[J]; // s.e. of effect estimates
}
parameters {
  real mu;
  real<lower=0> tau;
  vector[J] eta;
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[J] theta;
  theta <- mu + tau*eta;
  print("Theta is", theta);
}
model {
  eta ~ normal(0,1);
  y ~ normal(theta, sigma);
  print("y=", y, " and eta=", eta);
}

# the R driver code
library(rstan)
schools_dat <- list(J = 8, y = c(28,  8, -3,  7, -1,  1, 18, 12),
                    sigma = c(15, 10, 16, 11,  9, 11, 10, 18))
fit <- stan(file = '8schools.stan', data = schools_dat, iter = 100, chains = 1) # smaller run


Kind regards,
Seán

> > I have tried to restart, but the new iteration seems different than previous one and still waste time on warmup.
>
> If you restart with the same seed, you'll get the same results.
>
> The time spent on warmup isn't necessarily wasted --- see my last
> message.  It's critical to have the warmup converge before sampling.
>
> How many effective samples do you need?
>
> Also, if you send us your model code, we can perhaps help with
> tuning it for speed.
>
> - Bob
>
>

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] suggest a function that can consecutively save posterior samples before all iteration finished
parts:
No, but we should really have that. I've thought about it myself.
We want to also provide chain ID in case you're running in parallel.

Then we have to make sure they get some reasonable values when doing
optimization, using the standalone log prob functions, etc. Maybe -1?

I created a feature request, noting some of the to-be resolved issues:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/1166

- Bob
